methods.name: CPS-Prompt
methods.paper: Critical Patch-Aware Sparse Prompting with Decoupled Training for Continual Learning on the Edge
methods.kind: CODA-based rehearsal-free prompt method targeting training efficiency
methods.recommendation: Prioritize native port into the existing task-based efficiency track
methods.difficulty_estimate: Medium; estimate from static inspection, not measured engineering time
mechanisms: Full-token frozen query: CLS attention times value norm gives patch importance
Temperature softmax and multinomial sampling without replacement reduce patches in the joint prompt/head training phase
Full-patch no-grad features and classifier-only backward in the second phase

proposed_cifar_recipe.recipe_status: Proposed only; no executable plan or config changed

static_findings: E2 with phase_ratio=.4 yields zero sparse/prompt epochs; E3 is the minimum to exercise both phases
README prompt-only phase description differs from actual joint prompt/head training and paper Algorithm 2
Source parser defaults differ from paper CIFAR values; all three mechanism arguments must be explicit
Source supports Tiny/Small/Base geometry, but Base default timm weights are AugReg2 rather than the existing common AugReg checkpoint
Encoder is explicitly frozen; existing CODA may compute encoder gradients even though its optimizer excludes encoder parameters
Classifier phase retains prompt requires_grad flags and optimizer state despite no prompt gradients
Full-token query remains in training and evaluation; classifier phase and prompted inference also use full patches
Source scheduler marker differs from current Mammoth custom_scheduler integration
Source Jetson fallback adds current and average power readings; reuse the existing common measurement path instead
port_requirements: Keep meta_* lifecycle, class masking, original ten-task prompt allocation and task-boundary orthogonalization
Pin common local checkpoint path and SHA for each size; verify all canonical150 encoder tensors before training
Apply identical common preprocessing and checkpoint choices to native and independent source reference
Preserve positional indices and separate patch-sampling RNG/checkpoint state
Measure query, importance/sampling, both training phases, task boundaries and evaluation
Report actual gradients, optimizer membership and parameter storage separately
Use a separate frozen-CODA control if attributing gains specifically to CPS/DPCT; preserve existing CODA source behavior
methods.license_observation: MIT for CPS; retain notices/licenses of inherited Mammoth/CODA files
methods.dependencies_observed: Python3.12, torch2.6.0, torchvision0.21, timm0.9.8; do not replace current environment wholesale

methods.name: REP
methods.paper: REP: Resource-Efficient Prompting for Rehearsal-Free Continual Learning
methods.kind: Efficiency components composed with a host prompt method, rather than an independent prompt-pool algorithm
methods.recommendation: Conditional candidate; obtain a complete reference or explicitly approve paper-based reconstruction before implementing
methods.difficulty_estimate: High with the currently published source; estimate, not measured engineering time
mechanisms: Swift prompt selection using a compact pretrained query model and fixed random projection
Adaptive layer dropping (ALD), which skips layer computation rather than merely freezing weights
static_findings: Official GitHub tree has twelve files; no main/trainer/config/checkpoint pipeline is published there
Swift projection in Prompt/EPrompt uses a fixed1024 output and a lazily created plain tensor; HiDePrompt path omits that projection
HiDe/Dual ALD global_step is not advanced in the published path and update_state receives keep probability as its step argument
L2P ALD increments the counter per block and separates the updated theta from the schedule controller theta
AToM patch starts with r=0 and length=0; the published repository contains no runner that sets these values
Prefix patch treats the first five x tokens as prompts although prefix K/V are outside the x sequence
AToM block sends attn_size while Attention reads size
Source isinstance-based patching does not automatically match current Mammoth CODA/HiDe block classes
REP ALD model registrations are Large-only in the published file; generic Tiny/Small/Base constructors are not complete REP registrations
L2P Prompt.forward includes CUDA events and per-call synchronize; source measurement side effects require explicit handling
methods.static_findings_scope: Observed contracts in the public source; no failing forward/training run was performed and undisclosed author code was not assessed
methods.full_reference_availability_scope: Not obtained from current official GitHub HEAD; paper checklist mentions a code attachment, but public OpenReview attachment access was not verified
methods.suggested_host: REP-CODA if a faithful implementation/reference is secured; REP-HiDe is an alternative with additional TII/classifier adaptation accounting
methods.host_selection_status: Proposal only; excluded L2P/DualPrompt have not been restored

size_support.small_status: Additional adaptation requiring an explicit ALD threshold and common checkpoint choice
size_support.tiny_query_savings: Expected to be smaller when both query and main encoders are Tiny; an architecture-based inference, not a measurement

port_requirements: Choose one retained host method before adding experiment combinations
Define and verify query model construction, weights, feature dimensions and host prompt-key mapping
Register the fixed random projection as a persistent buffer and preserve its seed/checkpoint state
Resolve ALD step units, feedback state, keep schedule and deterministic evaluation behavior
Handle prefix K/V separately from x sequence tokens and validate prompt preservation and attention size semantics
Count auxiliary query parameters/storage, merging overhead and actual skipped blocks
Use matched host vs host+REP settings and distinguish source-behavior validation from paper-correct reconstruction
Do not claim the existing author/native accuracy gate has passed without an independent complete reference
methods.license_observation: Repository LICENSE is CC BY-NC4.0; preserve the separate conditions and attribution instead of assuming Mammoth MIT covers copied REP code
methods.dependencies_observed: README lists Python3.8.8, torch1.12.1/cu113, torchvision0.13.1, timm0.6.7; use isolated source references and native adaptation

comparison_notes: Prioritize CPS in the existing multi-epoch task-efficiency track; keep online/chunk budget protocols as separate tracks
Retain CODA as a matched host/control; REP variants must identify their host
Two-task pilots exercise mechanisms but do not reproduce full ten-task long-term retention
Reuse shared data/cache, local artifacts, WandB and Slack only when later implementation/experiment work is authorized
Jetson device energy and RTX4090 GPU-board energy are different measurement scopes; paper speedups are not local predictions
